To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the LHC can probe parton distribution functions at low x, (ii) the LHC will probe PDFs in a region that has not been measured before, (iii) the LHC measurements of PDFs in the low x domain can be used to constrain PDFs at the low x scale, which can be used in turn to make predictions for the LHC, and (iv) the measurements can be used in conjunction with other measurements to improve the knowledge of PDFs.

the LHC can measure the Drell–Yang production of low-masses lepton-pairs at high rapidities and, by imposing a transverse momentum cut, can make a direct determination of parton distribution function in the low x domain, x≲ 10−4.

the LHC can measure PDFs at low x, down to x≲10 −4, via a measurement of the Drell−Yan cross-section at low mass, M≲20  GeV, and high rapidity, Y≳3, and that this measurement can be made with a small theoretical error by imposing a cutoff of 5 GeV on the transverse mass of the lepton pair.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new way of probing the small x region of the parton density distributions of the proton.
the following: the Drell-Yan process, which is the production of lepton pairs in hadron-hadron collisions.

the study of the Drell−Yan production of lepton-pairs at the LHC in the region of low invariant masses, M≲20  GeV, and large rapidities, Y≳3, and how this process can be used as a probe of the small x partons in the proton.

the data are not yet able to constrain the gluon density at low x.

the LHC is a unique tool to study the low x physics.

we show that the measurement of the Drell−Yan cross section at high rapidities and low invariant mass at the LHC, with a transverse momentum cut, is an ideal probe for the low x region of the parton distribution functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the measurement of Drell–YAN at high rapidity at the LHC is a powerful tool for probing the small x gluon and the sea quarks at a low scale, and can provide important information about the low-x behavior of the PDFs.
, with a suitable choice of the transverse momentum cutoff, the Drell– Yan process at the LHC is a powerful probe of PDFs at low x and low scales.
a precise determination of the low-x gluon density can be made using the LHC Drell–YAN data.
